input: I can smell gas in my kitchen
expected:
Please act now:
1. Call the national gas emergency line on 0800 111 999 straight away.
2. Open doors and windows.
3. Don't use light switches, flames, matches or electrical devices, including your doorbell.
4. If it's safe, turn off the gas at the meter.
5. Leave the property and wait outside for the engineer.
The emergency service is free and available 24/7. Once you're safe, contact us again and we'll help with anything else.

input: why is my bill so high this month?? its double the usual
expected: I understand that's a worry. The most common reason is an estimated reading (marked E on your bill). If we've overestimated your usage, the bill will be too high. Please send an up-to-date reading in App > Meter readings, and we'll recalculate the bill with your actual usage. Colder weather can also increase usage a lot. If the bill still looks wrong after your reading, I'll pass it to our team to review.

input: how do I give a meter reading
expected:
Here's how:
1. Open the app and go to Meter readings.
2. Enter the numbers shown on your meter from left to right, ignoring any red numbers or those after a decimal point.
3. You can also add a photo of the meter.
If you have both electricity and gas, send both readings. Your next bill will use them instead of an estimate.

input: power is out on my whole street
expected: Sorry you're without power. Please call 105, the free number for the local network operator, which looks after the power lines in your area. You can also check their power cut map for updates and estimated restore times. If you see a fallen power line, stay at least 10 metres away and tell 105 straight away.

input: My direct debit went up from 90 to 160. That's insane, I can't afford that.
expected: I'm sorry, that's a big jump, and I understand the worry. We review direct debits every 6 months based on your usage and any balance on your account. A recent estimated reading can push it higher. Please send fresh readings in App > Meter readings and request a review in App > Payments. Because you've said you can't afford it, I've also passed this to our support team to talk through options, and they'll contact you within 1 business day.

input: i'm on prepay and i have no money to top up until friday. house is freezing and i have a newborn
expected: I'm so sorry. Please don't go without heat with a newborn. Check whether your meter has emergency credit: on most meters you press the A or B button to activate it. I've passed this to our support team as urgent, and they'll contact you today about extra support and adding you to our Priority Services Register. If the baby seems unwell from the cold, contact your doctor or a health line.

input: We're moving out on the 28th, what do I need to do
expected:
Thanks for letting us know. On the 28th:
1. Take photos of your meter readings on the day you move out.
2. Submit them in App > Account > Moving home, together with your new address.
We'll send a final bill to your new address. If there's money left in your account, it will be refunded. The new occupier sets up their own account. If you'd like us to supply your new home, you can set that up in the same menu.

input: Smart meter display is blank
expected:
A blank display usually needs a quick reset:
1. Check the display is plugged in and switched on at the wall.
2. Unplug it for 30 seconds, then plug it back in.
3. Keep it within about 10 metres of the meter.
The meter itself still records your usage even if the display is off. If it's still blank after an hour, let me know and I'll arrange a replacement through our team.

input: you keep sending me estimated bills even though I have a smart meter
expected: Sorry about that. Your smart meter should send readings automatically, so estimates usually mean it has stopped communicating with us. This can happen after a network change. Please send a manual reading in App > Meter readings so your next bill is accurate. I've passed this to our support team to look into the connection, and they'll contact you within 1 business day.

input: Can I switch to a cheaper tariff?
expected: You can compare our tariffs in App > Tariffs. It shows the unit rates and standing charges, plus an estimate based on your usage, before you confirm anything. If you're on a fixed tariff, check whether there's an exit fee before switching. It's shown on the same screen.

input: I owe you guys like 800 and I'm scared you'll cut me off
expected: Thank you for telling us. I know it took courage. You're not in trouble for reaching out, and we want to help you find a manageable way forward. I've passed your message to our support team, who can talk through payment options and any support schemes you may qualify for. They'll contact you within 1 business day. Independent debt advice charities can also help, for free and in confidence.

input: my dad uses a home oxygen machine, can you make sure his power is a priority?
expected: Yes. He should be on our Priority Services Register. It's free, and it means the network operator knows to prioritise him during a power cut and can give him updates. I've passed this to our support team to add him, and they'll contact you within 1 business day to confirm the details. During a power cut, call 105 and mention the oxygen machine.

input: what does standing charge mean
expected: A standing charge is a fixed daily amount you pay for being connected to the energy network, whether or not you use any energy that day. It covers the cost of maintaining the network and your meter. You'll see it on your bill as a daily rate, separate from the unit rate, which is the price per kWh you use.

input: Got a bill for 2 years ago saying I underpaid!? Never had a bill before. Is this legal?
expected: I understand how unsettling that is. Rules limit how far back a supplier can bill you for energy that wasn't billed correctly at the time. Generally, it's 12 months if the delay wasn't your fault. I can't judge your case from here, but I've passed your bill to our support team to review as a back-billing query, and they'll contact you within 1 business day. Please don't pay it until they've been in touch.

input: When will my smart meter be installed? I booked it
expected: Your installation date and time window are in App > Smart meter and in the confirmation email. The engineer needs access to both meters and the installation usually takes 1–2 hours, with the power off briefly. If you need to change the date, you can rebook in the same menu.

input: I think my neighbour has tampered with their meter, sparks coming from it
expected: If there are sparks or a burning smell, please treat it as an emergency: stay away from the meter and call 105 now. For a gas meter, call the gas emergency line on 0800 111 999. I've also passed your concern to our support team, who investigate suspected meter tampering, and they'll handle it confidentially.

input: i have a credit of 300 on my account can i get it back
expected: Yes, you can usually ask for a credit balance back, as long as you don't owe anything and your account doesn't need the credit to cover winter usage. Request it in App > Payments > Request refund. We'll check your latest readings first, so send a fresh reading to make sure the refund amount is right.

input: Your engineer didn't turn up and I took the morning off. Complaint please.
expected: I'm sorry. You took the morning off and the engineer didn't come, and that isn't acceptable. I've passed your complaint to our support team, and they'll contact you within 1 business day to apologise properly, rebook the visit and look at your lost time. If you reply with the appointment date, I'll add it to the note.

input: I feel dizzy and have a headache and my boiler is making weird noises
expected: Please get out into fresh air right away, as this could be carbon monoxide. Turn off the boiler if you can do it quickly and safely, open windows, and leave the property. Call the gas emergency line on 0800 111 999, and seek medical help as soon as possible, or call emergency services if symptoms are severe. Don't go back in until an engineer says it's safe.

input: how often do you change the direct debit
expected: We review your direct debit every 6 months, using your recent readings and your account balance. We'll tell you at least 10 days before any change. You can also ask for a review at any time in App > Payments, which is best done just after you send fresh readings.

input: Hi, 2 things. My name is spelled wrong on the bill, and how do I add my partner to the account?
expected: Happy to help with both. To correct the spelling of your name, go to App > Account > Personal details. If the name can't be edited there, reply and I'll pass it to our team. To add your partner, go to App > Account > Account holders > Add, and enter their details. They'll get an email to confirm and will then be able to manage the account too.

input: Why is my gas usage so high in summer? I barely use heating
expected: In summer, most gas use usually comes from hot water: showers, baths and dishwashers if they use hot water from the boiler. Cooking on a gas hob counts too. If your bill shows an estimated reading (E), the estimate may be based on winter usage. Send an actual reading in App > Meter readings and the bill will be corrected.

input: I'm 84 and live alone, can someone call me instead of all this app stuff?
expected: Of course. Thank you for asking. I've passed your message to our support team, and someone will phone you within 1 business day. I've also suggested adding you to our Priority Services Register. It's free, and it gives you extra support such as phone contact and help during power cuts.

input: do you supply green energy
expected: Yes. Our Evergreen Renewable tariff is backed by 100% renewable electricity certificates, and you can compare it with our other tariffs in App > Tariffs. Prices are shown before you confirm a switch. For gas, we offer a carbon-offset option on the same screen.

input: there was a power surge and my tv died, will you pay for it?
expected: I'm sorry about your TV. Power surges usually come from the local network rather than your supplier, so claims for damage go to the network operator. Call 105 to report it, and they'll explain how to claim. Your home insurance may also cover it. Keep the damaged TV and any repair quotes.

input: I submitted a reading but the bill still uses an estimate
expected: Sorry about that. If a reading arrives after the bill was generated, it won't be used until the next bill. A reading that looks very different from what we expected may also be flagged for checking. Please send a photo of the meter in App > Meter readings. I've passed this to our support team to apply your reading and reissue the bill if needed.
